candidates_dismissed.candidate: omitted_risk: Okta administrators as an access path outside the request process (P-397d12aece)
candidates_dismissed.why: The plan covers this risk. The LHP-01 PROV-A pass/fail states 'No control is described over manual Okta administrator changes'. Its evidence includes an Okta administrator role listing and System Log group membership add/remove events, and the D6 question asks for every path by which access is granted.

candidates_dismissed.candidate: contradictory_criterion: P-14735a8ee7/PROV-C narrative L13 vs policy L5
candidates_dismissed.why: On timing the two texts agree: narrative L13 says 'before the role is assigned' and policy L5 says 'before it is provisioned'. They differ only on who approves. That is PROV-B, which the plan already records as an open contradiction (P-14735a8ee7/approver). PROV-C is correctly shown as defined.

candidates_dismissed.candidate: contradictory_criterion: P-a40c9cf7e5/CHG-B narrative L21 vs policy L9
candidates_dismissed.why: These texts are consistent. Policy L9 requires that changes are 'tested and approved before they reach production'. Narrative L21 adds detail by naming sandbox testing with the requesting business user. The plan's CHG-B criterion from narrative L21 does not conflict with policy L9.

findings.rationale: Narrative L25 describes a ClaimsLens change control: required second-engineer PR approval with automated deployment on merge. The plan has no control for it and marks ClaimsLens/CM-CHG as an unresolved coverage gap. ClaimsLens is in scope and feeds the revenue accrual. Leaving the cell open leaves ClaimsLens change risk untested: branch-protection bypass, workflow alteration, untested changes, and AWS/database changes outside GitHub.

source.quote: The repository's branch protection requires a pull request approved by a second Cirrus Ops engineer before anything merges to main, and the GitHub Actions workflow deploys automatically on merge.

findings.suggested_action: Add a CM-CHG control for ClaimsLens citing narrative L25. Set CHG-C and CHG-D criteria from the L25 text only. Build CHG-A from GitHub Actions deployment runs traced to merged PRs. Inspect branch protection settings and the GitHub audit log for bypasses or admin overrides. List GitHub repository admins and AWS IAM users with production deploy rights for CHG-F. Record CHG-B (no testing criterion in L25), CHG-E and CHG-DE7 as design gaps with no criterion supplied. Raise the absence of a Cirrus Ops SOC report (narrative L25) for engagement-team decision.

findings.rationale: For ClaimsLens, the only approval described is a peer review by another engineer at Cirrus Ops, the service organisation. No Lumen approval is described, and Cirrus Ops provides no SOC report.

source.quote: requires a pull request approved by a second Cirrus Ops engineer before anything merges to main

findings.suggested_action: Pose to the engagement team: is approval of a pull request by a second Cirrus Ops engineer an authorized change approval for Lumen's financial reporting? Without a SOC report, what Lumen-side evidence or procedures are needed to rely on Cirrus Ops' GitHub and AWS controls?

findings.rationale: The plan's contradictions list shows the UAR-E timeframe as open, and its UAR-E procedure calls it an open contradiction. Yet the criterion table marks UAR-E as 'defined' at five business days from narrative L17. The two texts also count from different start points: L17 runs from the Controller's marking, L7 from the review. A tester could apply five days before the question is resolved.

source.quote: Access that is no longer required is removed within ten business days of the review.

findings.suggested_action: Change the UAR-E criterion status to 'contradiction open'. Record both texts with their start points. Ask the engagement team which governs, then set pass/fail. In the meantime, record actual removal dates against both the marking date and the review date.

findings.rationale: The plan marks UAR-C as 'contradiction open'. Its UAR-C pass/fail nonetheless states 'The reviewer must be the Controller (narrative L17)', which applies the narrative side before anyone has resolved the conflict with policy L7.

source.quote: Managers review the access of their staff to financial systems at least twice a year.

findings.suggested_action: Remove the Controller-only pass/fail until the reviewer contradiction is resolved. Meanwhile record the actual reviewer and whether the Controller's own NetSuite roles were reviewed by someone else. Pose to the engagement team: does a single Controller review satisfy policy L7's manager review of staff access?

findings.rationale: LHP-01 records PROV-C as an open 'approval_timing' contradiction, and PROV-B as 'not defined by control'. Neither narrative L11 nor policy L5 states a timing that conflicts with the other. The real issue is that baseline NetSuite roles and ClaimsLens accounts are granted with no per-request approval, while policy L5 requires manager or system-owner approval. As labelled, the plan blocks PROV-C on a contradiction that does not exist and hides the approval question.

source.quote: must be approved by the employee's manager or the system owner before it is provisioned

findings.suggested_action: Relabel the LHP-01 open item as an approver/authorization question under PROV-B and PROV-F, citing policy L5 and narrative L11. Pose to the engagement team: can an approved Workday-job-profile-to-Okta-group mapping rule set count as the policy L5 approval for baseline access, and if so, who must approve the rule set?

findings.rationale: The plan marks CHG-D and CHG-F as 'contradiction open', but its CHG-D and CHG-F pass/fail already apply policy L9. Narrative L21 ('The Finance Systems Manager both develops and deploys') describes a practice; it does not state a competing criterion. Treating this as a contradiction may delay a design-gap conclusion.

source.quote: Developers must not deploy their own changes to production unless a second person reviews the deployment.

findings.suggested_action: Pose to the engagement team: is policy L9 the governing criterion for NetSuite segregation, with narrative L21 describing a practice that departs from it? If so, record CHG-D and CHG-F as defined from policy L9 and route the narrative L21 practice to design evaluation instead of the contradiction log.

findings.rationale: The plan marks ClaimsLens/AC-PROV as 'tested under a module', relying only on LHP-01. The documents describe how ClaimsLens accounts are created, but not which ClaimsLens roles or permissions are assigned or how. No request and approval process for elevated ClaimsLens access is described. LHP-02 covers NetSuite and Jira only. A ClaimsLens PROV-D criterion therefore has no documentary basis, and ClaimsLens privileged access is not covered.

source.quote: Okta then creates, changes, or removes the person's NetSuite and ClaimsLens accounts

findings.suggested_action: Do not supply a ClaimsLens role criterion. Record PROV-D for ClaimsLens as not defined by the control. Add walkthrough questions on how ClaimsLens roles and admin rights are granted and by whom. Obtain a production ClaimsLens user/role listing. Reconsider whether ClaimsLens/AC-PROV should stay marked as tested or be shown as a partial coverage gap.

findings.rationale: LHP-02 is a manual Jira request and assignment process. PROV-F covers automated rule approval and belongs to LHP-01. Showing PROV-F as 'proposed, pending design confirmation' with a 'design finding raised' risks a duplicate design gap.

source.quote: Anything beyond the baseline, for example the AP clerk, AR specialist, or administrator roles in NetSuite, has to be requested in Jira.

findings.suggested_action: Mark PROV-F not applicable to P-14735a8ee7, with a reason. Keep rule-approval testing under P-397d12aece.

notes: Candidates: two confirmed. C5 is confirmed as an omitted control. The UAR-E candidate is confirmed but recast: the plan already logs the five-versus-ten-day contradiction, yet its criterion table shows UAR-E as defined at five days. Three candidates are dismissed: the Okta-administrator risk is already in the plan, and the PROV-C and CHG-B pairs are consistent texts rather than contradictions. Own findings: (1) the plan's UAR-C pass/fail adopts the narrative side of an open contradiction. (2) The LHP-01 'approval_timing' contradiction is mislabelled; the real question is whether an approved rule set meets policy L5. (3) The LHP-04 segregation issue is framed as a contradiction when it reads as a policy requirement against a described practice. (4) The ClaimsLens/AC-PROV cell is marked tested although ClaimsLens role assignment and elevated-access approval are undescribed. (5) PROV-F is applied to the manual Jira control. (6) For C5, whether Cirrus Ops engineers are authorized approvers needs a human decision. Not raised as a finding: NetSuite went live on 1 October 2025 (narrative L7) and the fiscal 2026 period dates are not stated. The engagement team should confirm whether a legacy system or a data migration falls in the period. I do not have the verbatim L7 text to cite. This review makes no effectiveness conclusion on any control.
